newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares rise 1.91 pct on renewed govt hopes.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares rise 1.91 pct on renewed govt hopes.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains on Thursday as market sentiment improved amid renewed hopes that a planned secularist coalition may survive a confidence vote in parliament, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed 32 points, or 1.91 percent higher at 1,705. Trade volume firmed to 19.33 trillion lira from Wednesday's 18.64 trillion.
A 14.65 trillion lira block deal was made on the wholesale market for the sale of Yapi Kredi Bank's shares to foreign investors.

"The rise was a reaction to (Prime Minister-Designate) Mesut Yilmaz's comments on his planned alliance. But prices may ease in coming days because there is still uncertainty over the confidence vote," said Haldun Sertel from Can securities.
"Uncertainty will grip the market until the political developments become clear," he added.

Conservative opposition leader Yilmaz said on Thursday President Suleyman Demirel had vowed to approve a planned coalition that would keep the ruling Islamist Welfare Party out of power, despite its current lack of a majority.

"The president told me he would approve a government with the support of four parties," Yilmaz told a news conference in reference to four opposition parties, currently short of a majority in the 550-seat parliament.
Yilmaz is due to submit a cabinet list early next week to Demirel, who has to approve the bid before it goes to parliament for a confidence vote.

Brokers said the defection of an anti-Islamist MP from Tansu Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) to Yilmaz's Motherland Party on Thursday also raised hopes in the market that the new pact could win the vote.

Yilmaz has won the backing of two left-wing parties, a secularist small right-wing grouping and a few conservative independents, but needs the support of around a dozen MPs from the rival DYP to win the vote.
Ciller who is allied with the Islamist Welfare, has rejected Yilmaz's offer to join his planned alliance.

Of the 243 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 152 to 39 and 52 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN lost 1.17 percent to 1,609, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ soared 3.11 percent to 1,756 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL dived 3.31 percent to 1,811.

Top actives were bluechips -- utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 242,500, largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli, up 1,000 lira at 23,250, utilities Aktas Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 232,500 and Kepez Elektrik, up 20,000 lira at 310,000. They made up 38.5 percent of the total turnover.
